lessons: Expert MAJOR deferred: no fallback path when Form 106 is unobtainable (defunct employer, employer refusing, older years). The standard workaround is the ITA rikuz netunim / ishur nikuyim withholding summary from the taxpayer personal area, which is also what the online refund portal auto-populates from. Note it does NOT reliably carry the 218/219 keren hishtalmut fields, so document what it does and does not replace. Step 6 currently states Form 106 from every employer as an absolute.

Expert MAJOR deferred: married-couple mechanics absent. Sections 64/65/66 are cited once and never explained. The estimator takes ONE salary and ONE points figure, so a couple running household totals through it gets a materially wrong answer with no warning. Add an explicit one-claim-per-spouse / never-aggregate instruction and the chishuv nifrad default.

Expert MAJOR deferred: ichud tikim never mentioned. If the spouse is self-employed or already holds a tik, the assessing officer works the file as a couple and the refund can be offset against the spouse's balance. Add a spouse question to the Step 1 gate and to the Gotchas offset bullet.

Expert MAJOR deferred: Example 1 shows only the no-Form-101-at-all archetype (47% flat at the second employer). The more common real Form 106 shows a 101 filed with the 'not my only income' box ticked, ordinary brackets and zero credit points, which yields roughly 40-41k withheld and a 16-20k refund rather than 37-45k. Show both variants, or state which box on the 101 produces which, so client expectations are not set about 2x too high.

Expert MINOR deferred: the estimator still applies the 3% earned-income mas yesafim above ~721,560 even though a salaried person at that income is generally 1301-obligated and routed out by Step 7. Harmless but note it in the docstring so surtax support is not read as a claim to cover high earners.
Expert MINOR deferred: Section 45A self-deposit case can double-count, because the 45A credit and the Section 47 deduction share a ceiling with the employer deposit leg.
Expert MINOR deferred: nothing tells the filer a refund can be claimed in a year with income below the tax threshold, or that no accountant or representative is required to file Form 135.

Process lesson: the per-year refactor renamed CREDIT_POINT_VALUE_ANNUAL_2026 to CREDIT_POINT_ANNUAL_BY_YEAR but missed one call site in the miluim print path, so every --miluim-days run crashed with NameError. The smoke test exercised --year across all years but never passed --miluim-days. Exercise EVERY declared flag after a constant rename, not just the ones in the changed code path.

Section 11(b1) azor kav imut dromi (20% up to 241,080 NIS in the nevo consolidated text) was NOT encoded: the ITA 2026 published table's 20% rows are 259,920 and 267,840, and the two figures could not be reconciled at source. Re-check against next year's booklet.
